title: W006 control implementation rollout from W005 interaction spine
description:
W006 rollout epic: carry W005's normalized input, reducer/effects, event facts, coordinate model, lifecycle/pump model, trace/replay schema, and evidence posture into implementation work without over-claiming full MSForms parity.

Start by reading docs/worksets/W006_control_implementation_rollout.md, then the W005 workset closure summary and W005 focused specs.

Dependency doctrine: the first ready W006 child is oxforms-0a0.9, the planning/review/rollout-hardening bead. Implementation and design child beads depend on that gate and must not begin from the broad residual list alone.

W006 preserves these non-claims until dedicated beads prove otherwise: no full UserForm/control parity, no pixel-perfect rendering parity, no runtime accessibility semantics, no native FM20-named OxVba dispatch, and no final pass/fail parity oracle.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- The W006 workset doc, register row, and bead graph identify oxforms-0a0.9 as the planning/review gate.
- Implementation/design child beads remain blocked on oxforms-0a0.9 until the rollout is hardened.
- Each executable child bead has scope, start-reading pointers, relevant docs, acceptance criteria, and the required fresh-eyes review/rework instruction.
- W006 closes only when the workset closure conditions in docs/worksets/W006_control_implementation_rollout.md are actually satisfied.
close_reason: W006 control-implementation rollout complete: all child beads implemented or precisely blocked with evidence. Live MSForms oracle captures (nested-modal 42 rows, DoEvents reentrancy, terminate held-ref + narrowed blocked paths, CheckBox Click-vs-Change oracle-confirmed value-change-first, text-service/clipboard/drag-drop); precise blockers preserved as non-claims (native FM20 OxVba dispatch, IME/dead-key, runtime accessibility); Rust follow-ups landed (mau, p41); process template (sut). title: Capture + honor the drag-drop-origin BeforeDropOrPaste Cancel veto
description: Follow-up from the oxforms-esq.17 review. esq.17 made the keyboard Ctrl+V paste two-stage so a vetoing BeforeDropOrPaste (Cancel=True) is honored (insert deferred until the Cancel readback folds back as BeforeDropOrPasteCompleted; gated on pending_paste_commit). The DRAG-DROP origin path (reduce_drop_or_paste in crates/oxforms-core/src/lib.rs) still inserts text SYNCHRONOUSLY before firing BeforeDropOrPaste and never sets pending_paste_commit, so its Cancel is recorded-not-honored. This is a deliberate esq.17 scope call (the oracle w008-paste-veto is a keyboard Ctrl+V; the drag-drop-origin veto is uncaptured) but is an asymmetry: the shared fixture handler InputField_BeforeDropOrPaste fires for both origins yet only takes effect for the keyboard path. Scope: (1) capture a vetoing drag-drop BeforeDropOrPaste against the live Excel/MSForms oracle (needs the live desktop); (2) if it suppresses the drop, route reduce_drop_or_paste through the same two-stage defer (pending_paste_commit) so the drag-drop veto is honored too + tests. title: W007 production runtime vertical slice
description:
W007 production runtime vertical-slice epic. Scope: create the first runnable, production-shaped OxForms/OxVba slice where an OxVba project loads the OxForms VBA library, creates a small form with Label, TextBox, and CommandButton controls, shows it in a real Windows window, accepts typed text and button input, runs native VBA event handlers, and updates a Label from VBA code.

Selected entry shape: Tiny Bootstrap. The bootstrap executable may load the OxVba project, configure OxVba/OxForms runtime services, invoke the VBA entrypoint, enter the runtime pump, and exit on no open forms or fatal diagnostics. It must not hard-code controls, mutate form state directly, dispatch user events through a custom callback API, contain demo-specific form logic, or become a long-term host framework.

Durable owner boundaries:
- VBA OxForms library owns MSForms-shaped UserForm/Label/TextBox/CommandButton classes, properties, and event declarations.
- OxVba owns class construction, RaiseEvent/WithEvents, handler dispatch, call-stack reentry, and future modal Show/DoEvents suspension-resume behavior.
- oxforms-core owns reducer state, ordered effects, invalidation, and display-list intent.
- OxForms runtime/effect-runner owns queues, effect execution, OxVba dispatch calls, property sync, completion rows, trace causality, and repaint requests.
- PAL/window backend owns native surfaces, physical OS message delivery, input normalization, rendering, and serializable completions.

title: Batched MeasureText: one crossing for all runs needing (re)measurement
description: RENDERING_ARCHITECTURE.md §6 specifies MeasureText(batch) -> metrics[] + TextRunId[] — ONE crossing for all runs needing (re)measurement. Today MeasureText is per-text-control (UserForm.EmitControl calls Surface.MeasureText once per control), so first paint of N text controls = BeginScene + N MeasureText + SubmitPatch = N+2 crossings. The §6 P6 target (50-control first paint ~ 3-5 crossings, independent of control count) needs the batched call: collect all controls' (font,size,caption) in the measure pass, cross once, distribute the id+metrics back. Steady-state (one keystroke) is already independent of N (rq5.2; gated by oxvba_surface_render_smoke::keystroke_crossing_count_is_independent_of_control_count). This bead closes the FIRST-PAINT side of the §6 budget. Locked/documented by first_paint_crossings_scale_with_text_controls_pending_batched_measuretext.
close_reason: Batched MeasureBatch implemented via typed VBA UDT records <-> VT_RECORD SAFEARRAY (Design A, panel-chosen on merit). title: Re-benchmark + settle hit-test home after OxVba vm3 array fix
description: UNBLOCKED: Cargo.toml is now pinned to an OxVba baseline that includes the round-2 vm3 class-field dynamic-array element-access fix (O(1) array reads), and docs/specs/HIT_TEST_AND_MESSAGE_LOOP_OFFLOAD.md already records the post-fix curve: per-array-read flat ~3.9us and linear HitTestAll at ~33us/control. Remaining scope: run the explicit ignored probe when settling routing/perf work ('cargo test -p oxforms-oxvba-adapter --test oxvba_lex_hittest_bench -- --ignored --nocapture'), record any fresh numbers, then decide indexed VBA pick vs Rust Scene pick under a per-frame budget. Working assumption remains indexed VBA pick first; Rust geometric pick is fallback if representative indexed numbers miss budget. This is now a W009 phase-0 perf/hit-test input, not an OxVba blocker.
close_reason: Settled the post-vm3-fix hit-test home for W009 broad controls. Extended the ignored OxVba hit-test probe with a layout-built VBA grid index, steady indexed pick measurement, index-build timing, and a frame-budget JSON artifact at docs/evidence/W009_first_class_runtime_foundation/perf/w009-hittest-home-settlement-20260707.json. Fresh numbers confirm class-field array access remains O(1), reject naïve VBA linear hit-testing for broad forms, and accept VBA-owned indexed picking as the next implementation home: steady pick stays 69-96 us from 50 to 400 controls under a 16.6 ms frame budget, while index rebuild is layout/visibility/z-order invalidation work only. Rust Scene picking remains the measured fallback if real invalidation churn later misses budget. Fresh-eyes review documented the important limitation: the fixture proves a grid/cell index and the ownership boundary, not the final arbitrary-rectangle production index. title: W002 initial Windows PAL rectangle smoke
description:
W002 workset epic: Initial Windows PAL rectangle smoke.

Goal: drive the first executable OxForms slice from plan to evidence. This workset proves the architecture direction by having a VBA app project load the OxForms VBA library, create a smoke-only OxForms form-like object, let the library create a host-injected OxForms smoke canvas through OxVba's portable COM-like projection, call a minimal FillRect display-list command through that object, have an OxVba adapter map that call into the OxForms PAL core, have Rust render it headlessly with stable diagnostics, and have a Windows visible smoke path paint the same command.

Read first:
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md, especially Purpose, Non-goals, Architecture Slice, Closure Condition, Verification Shape, Risks And Controls, and the oxforms-dwm.7 through oxforms-dwm.10 repair notes.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md decisions D2, D8, D9, D10, sections 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 6.2, 9, 10.2, and the W002 bootstrap slice in section 11.
- docs/SOURCE_REFERENCES.md section OxVba Development Baseline for pinned dependency policy.
- docs/evidence/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md Structural Coupling Repairs.

Non-goals for the whole epic: do not implement full UserForm.Show, .frm/.frx parsing, intrinsic controls, text metrics, input routing, timers, clipboard, image decode, or MSForms parity claims. The smoke API is temporary and must be named/treated as smoke-only.
design:
Execution model:
1. oxforms-dwm.1 finishes the self-contained bead/workset plan.
2. oxforms-dwm.2 scaffolds the Rust/VBA workspace using the pinned OxVba dependency policy.
3. oxforms-dwm.3 implements DisplayList/FillRect and a deterministic headless renderer.
4. oxforms-dwm.4 initially proved VBA execution with a weak Debug.Print trace path.
5. oxforms-dwm.5 adds a Windows visible smoke path from the same display list.
6. oxforms-dwm.6 records evidence and closes the first pass.
7. oxforms-dwm.7 repairs the coupling: VBA uses CreateObject("OxForms.SmokeCanvas"), calls CreateSurface/FillRect/Flush, and Rust renders on Flush.
8. oxforms-dwm.8 repairs the ownership direction: OxVba loads an app .basproj plus referenced OxForms.basproj; the app creates an OxForms smoke form; the OxForms library owns the PAL canvas bridge.
9. oxforms-dwm.9 repairs the adapter naming: the Rust module is named oxvba_pal_adapter so it reads as an OxVba-facing PAL adapter, not as Rust hosting VBA.
10. oxforms-dwm.10 repairs the crate layering: oxforms-pal is host/runtime independent, while oxforms-oxvba-adapter owns PortableDispatch, Variant marshalling, projection registration, and the OxVba smoke test.

Headless rendering is the automated oracle; visible Windows rendering is important but should not become a flaky CI gate. The repaired OxVba proof is app project -> OxForms VBA library -> OxVba adapter -> PAL core renderer, not stdout/string parsing and not OxVba embedded in the PAL core.
acceptance_criteria:
The epic is complete only when:
- oxforms-dwm.2 through oxforms-dwm.10 are closed with their acceptance checks satisfied.
- The Rust PAL renders a FillRect display list headlessly with stable checked diagnostics/hash.
- The OxVba-driven VBA smoke loads RectangleSmokeApp.basproj plus referenced OxForms.basproj, and the app does not directly create OxForms.SmokeCanvas.
- The OxForms VBA library creates/accesses a host-injected OxForms.SmokeCanvas and reaches the Rust PAL core through the OxVba adapter by calling CreateSurface, FillRect, and Flush.
- The VBA smoke proof does not rely on Debug.Print/stdout-style trace strings as the coupling mechanism.
- oxforms-pal contains no OxVba dependencies; OxVba-specific PortableDispatch/Variant marshalling lives in oxforms-oxvba-adapter.
- The Windows visible smoke exists and is verified on Windows, or a concrete blocker/follow-up bead records why it could not be verified.
- Evidence records commands, artifacts, hashes, platform notes, and fresh-eyes review outcome.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md and docs/WORKSET_REGISTER.md accurately describe final status.
notes:
Dependency: W002 depends on oxforms-rzk / W001 repo bootstrap. Do not start implementation beads until W001 and oxforms-dwm.1 are closed.

Review rule for every child bead: At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.
close_reason: Reclosed W002 after oxforms-dwm.11: smoke projection is module-scoped, PAL core is host-neutral, and checks/evidence confirm the final architecture.

title: W008 fold Return* readbacks back into reducer state (swallow/veto feedback)
description: Native FM20 dispatch (oxforms-esq.2) RECORDS each Return* readback in NativeDispatchRecord.returned but does not yet FOLD IT BACK into reducer state: a swallowed KeyDown/KeyUp KeyCode or KeyPress KeyAscii (post-handler 0) does not suppress the downstream KeyPress/Change/character insertion; a vetoed focus [Exit] (Cancel=True) does not roll back the focus commit (focus still commits synchronously); a vetoed QueryClose (Cancel nonzero) does not cancel the close (the runtime would need to synthesize a QueryCloseCompleted with cancelled=true and re-reduce so reduce_query_close_completed routes to CloseCancelled instead of HideForm). Also tracks the focus Enter gap (not emitted/dispatched; needs a new control Enter event + PerformEnter + reducer emission). Acceptance: each fold-back path proven by a committed reducer+runtime test (swallowed key suppresses downstream; vetoed Exit keeps focus; vetoed QueryClose cancels the close), or carries a precise blocker. title: W003 Excel Forms oracle and Windows capture plumbing
description:
W003 workset epic: Excel Forms oracle and Windows capture plumbing.

Goal: create the first reproducible black-box oracle path against real Microsoft Forms running inside Excel/VBA, so future OxForms rendering work has a measured target instead of guessing. W003 should produce a tiny real Excel UserForm fixture, a Windows capture/discovery harness, durable artifacts, and the first comparison manifest that points from the Excel oracle toward OxForms outputs.

Read first:
- CHARTER.md sections 3 and 4 for compatibility-first and clean-room constraints.
- OPERATIONS.md sections 7 and 8 for evidence and handover expectations.
- docs/worksets/W003_excel_forms_oracle_capture.md once created, especially Purpose, Non-goals, Architecture Slice, Closure Condition, Verification Shape, and Risks And Controls.
- docs/evidence/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md for the existing OxForms rectangle baseline.

Non-goals for W003: do not implement .frm/.frx ingestion, UserForm.Show in OxForms, intrinsic controls in OxForms, pixel-exact matching, wasm/Tauri/web backends, broad UI Automation coverage, or Office-internal reverse engineering. W003 is an oracle/capture workset, not a renderer expansion.
design:
Execution model:
1. oxforms-fg9.3 writes and commits the W003 workset plan/register/bead graph.
2. oxforms-fg9.1 scaffolds an oracle harness and fixture/artifact layout.
3. oxforms-fg9.2 implements reusable Windows discovery/capture primitives.
4. oxforms-fg9.4 creates the first real Excel UserForm oracle fixture.
5. oxforms-fg9.5 combines the fixture and capture primitives to produce durable Excel oracle artifacts.
6. oxforms-fg9.6 defines the first oracle comparison artifact format and seeds a calibration comparison against existing OxForms outputs where possible.
7. oxforms-fg9.7 records evidence, reviews the whole workset, updates docs, and closes W003 only if objective closure conditions are met.

The graph intentionally puts the oracle before broader backend architecture. Other backends should be tracked as constraints, but not built, until the Excel/MSForms measuring stick exists.

The epic is complete only when:
- oxforms-fg9.1 through oxforms-fg9.7 are closed with their acceptance checks satisfied.
- A real Excel/VBA UserForm oracle fixture exists and is generated or opened reproducibly from repo-owned inputs.
- Windows capture/discovery records at least window identity, bounds, screenshot pixels, platform/Excel version notes, and useful logs for that fixture.
- Artifacts live under docs/evidence or another documented artifact path with stable manifests/checksums.
- A first comparison manifest describes how the Excel oracle output relates to the current OxForms W002 rectangle output or explicitly records why exact comparison is deferred.

- No committed artifact or process violates clean-room rules.

title: W010 complete MSForms full-library parity sweep
description:
W010 executes a deep, mechanically tracked parity sweep of the complete accepted callable Microsoft Forms 2.0 library beyond W009's explicitly limited subset depth. Scope includes UserForm and the intrinsic global UserForms collection; Control/Controls; all fourteen intrinsic controls; Page/Pages and Tab/Tabs; Font/NewFont, stdole Picture/IPictureDisp, DataObject and all Return* helpers; every enum/alias; exact public and versioned coclass/interface identity; default members; properties, setters, methods, source events, errors/coercions, rendering effects, and .frm/.frx persistence. The full FM20 typelib plus referenced public typelibs, Foundation's pinned public MS-OFORMS mirror, independently captured .frm/.frx export facts, public Microsoft documentation, and reproducible black-box Office/MSForms observations are the allowed ground truth.

The compatibility perimeter also includes the actual FM20 HTMLSubmit, HTMLImage, HTMLReset, HTMLCheckbox, HTMLOption, HTMLText, HTMLHidden, HTMLPassword, HTMLSelect, and HTMLTextArea families and their versioned identities, and callable hidden/non-browsable members. A row may be excluded only with authoritative evidence that it is non-callable, restricted, or implementation-only; HTML/versioned rows cannot close by classification alone when callable. In particular, DesignMode, ShowToolbox, ShowGridDots, SnapToGrid, GridX, GridY, and DrawBuffer are probed and implemented wherever callable. The interactive designer UI, arbitrary third-party ActiveX internals, Excel RefEdit, and OxDoc-owned binary MS-OFORMS container conversion remain out of scope.

Closure requires a generated row-level conformance ledger with no missing, partial, unknown, prose-only, unexpected-public, or accepted-blocked-as-done rows anywhere in the accepted full-library perimeter. Exact signatures/default members/type identity, behavior, coercion/errors, events, rendering, and persistence require tests and evidence. An external OxVba/platform limitation is handed over and keeps the owning row/bead open or precisely blocked; it never becomes a completed parity claim.

title: Prove VBA-side reducer/interaction feasibility on OxVba vm3
description: Per the 2026-06-29 decision (memory: oxforms-reducer-home-decision), the intended design moves control interaction/behavior (the reducer) out of the Rust oxforms-core crate into VBA, running on OxVba vm3, with the runtime path input -> VBA reduce -> effects -> oxforms-pal (Scene/Prim kernel), no Rust reducer in the path. Before committing to the full port, PROVE FEASIBILITY with a minimal spike: a VBA-authored interaction step for ONE control (e.g. a value toggle / keystroke / hit-test+focus) that drives a state change + Scene re-render through the pal kernel on vm3, with NO Rust reducer involved. Capture a note on perf/shape feasibility: per-input reduce cost, fit with the OxVba event spine, and any OxVba gaps (which become OxVba closure tasks per FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN §9). ACCEPTANCE: a runnable spike OR a precise blocker that establishes whether the VBA-reducer design is viable on vm3. Workset-INDEPENDENT (not under W009 or the reducer-pivot epic). If feasible -> follow-up PORTING bead migrates the existing 4 controls' behavior (Label/CommandButton/TextBox/CheckBox) to VBA and deletes oxforms-core. Refs: FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN §4.2/§4.3/§9; W009 doc; memory oxforms-reducer-home-decision.
close_reason: FEASIBLE. title: Codify long-term architecture doctrine
description:
Codify OxForms long-term development architecture doctrine so future work does not preserve temporary bridge/fallback shapes as implementation patterns.

Start by reading:
- CHARTER.md sections 1, 3, 5, and 6.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md decisions D2, D7, D8, D10 and sections 4.1, 6, 9, and 11.
- docs/worksets/W002_initial_windows_rectangle.md final proved scope and closure condition.

Scope:
- Explain and correct the D2 wording: the OxVba path is injected host objects because that is the current best canonical integration shape, not because OxForms is maintaining backward compatibility with a bridge.
- Establish in the charter/spec that initial OxForms development has no internal backward-compatibility obligation to temporary smoke APIs, bridge APIs, or legacy integration paths.
- State the durable constraints: MSForms/FM20 behavioral and visual compatibility, long-term state-of-the-art internal architecture, future extreme optimization, cross-platform robustness, and maintainability.
- State that temporary scaffolding must be deleted, replaced, or explicitly quarantined before it can become a pattern for later work.
- Update live bead state and run documentation/graph checks.

Non-goals:
- Do not change runtime behavior in this bead.
- Do not implement new PAL bindings, C ABI exports, COM surfaces, or backend code.
- Do not weaken D2; clarify it.
design: This is a cross-cutting doctrine bead. It protects the project from accidental legacy buildup during bootstrap: smoke APIs, temporary bridges, alternate host bindings, and compatibility shims must not become examples to copy. The only compatibility target is MSForms/FM20 behavior and output, not previous OxForms internal shapes.
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance criteria:
- CHARTER.md explicitly states that internal development-era APIs/bridges have no backward-compatibility protection and must yield to the long-term optimal architecture.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md D2 and workspace layout clearly define one canonical PAL contract with runtime-specific injected-object adapters, and clarify that any alternate binding must be first-class and generated/mechanical from the same contract rather than a legacy fallback.
- W002 evidence or workset docs no longer suggest native/C ABI fallback is a compatibility bridge to preserve.
- Relevant checks pass: read-through/path scan, git diff --check, br dep cycles, and br ready --json.
- Commit docs/bead state with this bead ID in the message.
notes:
This bead intentionally blocks W003 starter beads while it is open, so the next work reads the clarified doctrine.

At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.
close_reason: Codified initial-development architecture doctrine: one canonical PAL contract, injected-object OxVba adapter, and no protected legacy/fallback internal paths.

title: W005 input and interaction model exploration
description:
W005 workset epic: Wide input and interaction model exploration.

Goal: settle the durable OxForms input/event architecture before broad control implementation. W005 covers normalized platform input, FM20 event signature/argument facts, coordinate systems/calibration, form lifecycle/modal pump behavior, hit-testing, focus/tab traversal, mouse capture, keyboard and character routing, accelerator/default/cancel behavior, validation/event ordering, reducer effects, trace/replay, MSForms oracle event observations, and the first interactive probes around Label, CommandButton, and TextBox.

Read first:
- CHARTER.md sections 1, 3, 3.1, 4, 5, and 7.
- OPERATIONS.md sections 4, 5, 7, and 10.
- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md decisions D1, D7, D8, D10, D11, D12; sections 4.3, 4.5, 5.3, 5.4, 6.2, 8, 9, 10.2, and P2 in section 11.
- docs/worksets/W004_text_label_oracle_pixels.md and W004 evidence as the first text oracle input.

Non-goals for W005: do not implement the full MSForms control set, do not complete full .frm/.frx persistence, do not claim pixel-perfect rendering parity, do not build non-Windows backends, and do not fork a forms-only event runtime if OxVba shared event machinery needs repair.
design: W005 is deliberately a wide architecture exploration, not a tiny text-rendering calibration. It should produce enough executable and documentary evidence that later control implementation can proceed on a stable interaction spine. The first control probes are chosen to force the main interaction axes: Label for non-focus text and mouse events, CommandButton for focus/click/default/cancel/accelerator behavior, and TextBox for keyboard, character input, text mutation, selection/caret basics, and Change/validation ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
The epic is complete only when:
- A W005 workset document and register row define the full interaction exploration scope and closure conditions.
- A spec surface or equivalent design document records the normalized UiEvent, FormState, Effects, focus/capture, event dispatch, coordinate, lifecycle/pump, and trace/replay model decisions produced by W005.
- FM20/MSForms event signature/argument facts and coordinate calibration evidence exist, or exact blocker beads explain missing public evidence/tooling.
- MSForms oracle fixtures or blocker beads exist for representative mouse, keyboard, focus, validation, lifecycle, and event-order observations.
- OxForms has an implemented or explicitly blocked first interaction substrate sufficient to replay a small interactive scenario through Label, CommandButton, and TextBox probes.
- Trace/replay artifacts exist for at least one interaction script and are suitable as regression evidence.
- Residual work discovered during exploration is filed as follow-up beads before closure.
notes: Review rule for every child bead: At the end of the bead, check over everything again with fresh eyes, looking for any blunders, mistakes, errors, oversights, omissions, logical issues, problems, misconceptions, confusion, bugs, etc. and rework accordingly. Then repeat the review - after there are no more issues raised by such a review, do a commit of the work.

- docs/FORMS_LIBRARY_SPEC_AND_PLAN.md sections 4.3, 4.5, 5.3, 5.4, 6.2, 8, 9, 10.2, 11/P2, and 12.

Scope:

- Define normalized UiEvent families: mouse move/down/up/double-click/wheel, keyboard down/up, character input, focus in/out, activation/deactivation, close request, timer, clipboard/service responses, DPI/resize, and host-extension events.
